body.p: Claims 60-79 are pending in the application. Claims 60-64, 66, and 67 are currently amended. Claims 68-79 are canceled without prejudice. New claims 80-91 are added. No new matter or issues are introduced by the claim amendments.

In view of the Restriction Requirement, withdrawn claims 68-79 are canceled without prejudice. The Applicant reserves the right to file a divisional application to prosecute the withdrawn/canceled claims. It is to be noted that withdrawn claims 63 and 64 are currently amended in anticipation of such claims being rejoined upon allowance of the application, given that independent claim 60 remains generic with regard to withdrawn claims 63 and 64. Moreover, it is to be noted that new claims 80-91 are believed to fall within the scope of the restriction requirement, as the subject matter of new claims 80-91 corresponds to the subject matter of claims 60-62, 65, and 66.

The Applicant would like to thank Examiner Catherine Voorhees for the telephone interview conducted on December 27, 2024 with the undersigned attorney. The Applicant gratefully acknowledges the Examiner's indication that the claim amendments are sufficient to overcome the claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 112 (second paragraph), 102 and 103 and that a further search and consideration will be given to determine if the claims are in condition for allowance. After further consideration, if the Examiner believes that additional clarifying amendments would advance the prosecution of this application to an allowance, the Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to contact the undersigned attorney to discuss such amendments.

With regard to claim 67, the Office Action contends that the use of neural network to process time series data is not disclosed in the priority provisional application. The Applicant respectfully notes that the claim features of claim 67 are in fact disclosed in the priority provisional application (see, e.g., paragraph [0043] and FIG. 1, block 132 of the priority provisional application). Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully asserts that the features of claim 67 should be accorded an effective filing date of May 8, 2019 based on the priority provisional application.

The Office Action construes certain claim limitations as being "means plus function" language, for the reasons noted on pages 2-4 of the Office Action. While the Applicant respectfully disagrees with such claim interpretation, it is respectfully submitted that claims as amended include claim terms which cannot be fairly characterized as generic placeholders, as stated in the Office Action. In this regard, the scope of the claims as amended should not be construed to fall under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f).

Claims 65-67 are rejected as being indefinite for the reasons noted on pages 4 and 5 of the Office Action. The Office Action contends that the recited claim features (i) compute a trend line for at least one extracted feature of the plurality of extracted features based on time series data collected for the at least one extracted feature, and (ii) risk stratify the computed trend line based on a result of comparing of the computed trend line with the known trend lines, renders claim 65 indefinite (and thus claims 66 and 67 by dependency) because the specification allegedly does not disclose an algorithm for performing the recited functions. The Applicant respectfully disagrees with these rejections, and contends that the subject matter of claim 65 is clear and definite in scope, and supported by the written description of the specification as filed.

For example, support for the claim limitation compute a trend line for at least one extracted feature of the plurality of extracted features based on time series data collected for the at least one extracted feature, can be found, e.g., in FIG. 10 and paragraph [0145] of the specification as filed. In particular, FIG. 10 illustrates a trend line graph 1010 which includes a plot of (i) time series data 1012 of normalized PR interval values that are determined from multiple cardiac cycles within a self-similar group of cardiac cycles, and (ii) a computed trend line 1014 of the normalized PR interval values. The specification specifically teaches that in some embodiments, the trend line 1014 is computed from the time series data 1012 of normalized PR interval values using a median filtering process. Median filtering techniques are non-linear digital filtering techniques that are well known and understood by those of ordinary skill in the art.

Moreover, support for the claim limitation risk stratify the computed trend line based on a result of comparing of the computed trend line with the known trend lines, can be found, e.g., in FIG. 13 and paragraphs [0150] and [0151] of the specification as filed, which provide clear and extensive written description to support the subject matter of claim 65. Accordingly, withdrawal of the 112 rejections is respectfully requested.

Claims 60-62 and 65-67 are rejected as being directed to non-statutory subject matter for the reasons noted on page 6 of the Office Action. While the Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection, the claim amendments are believed to have rendered this rejection moot on the ground that the subject matter of the amended claims cannot reasonably be characterized as covering mental processes, as acknowledged by the Examiner during the telephone interview. Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 101 is respectfully requested.
The following rejections are currently asserted:
(i) Claims 60 and 62 are rejected as being anticipated by Bashour et al (U.S. 2008/0167567);
(ii) Claim 61 is rejected as being unpatentable over Bashour in view of Ong et al. (U.S. 2011/0224565);
(iii) Claims 65 and 67 are rejected as being unpatentable over Bashour in view of the non-patent literature reference by Kimura-Medorima; and
(iv) Claim 66 is rejected as being unpatentable over Bashour and Kimura-Medorima, and further in view of Sharma et al. (U.S. 2016/0038093).

The Applicant respectfully traverses the claim rejections on the ground that currently asserted references do not disclose or suggest limitations of the rejected claims. Notwithstanding, the claims have been amended for the sole purpose of expediting the prosecution of this application to an allowance. In this regard, the specific obviousness rejections are rendered moot in view of claim amendments, as acknowledged by the Examiner during the telephone interview. Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103 is respectfully requested.

By this amendment, the Applicant is not disclaiming the scope of the original claims, and the Applicant is not conceding that the subject matter encompassed by the original claims is unpatentable over the currently asserted art. The Applicant reserves the right to prosecute the original claims, and other subject matter, in one or more continuation applications. Again, this amendment is made for the sole purpose of expediting the prosecution of this application to an allowance.
In this regard, it is to be noted that the Applicant generally denies, and does not concede to, any statements, positions, or averments in the Office Action in support of the claim rejections,
which are not specifically addressed by the foregoing arguments and response. The Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the claim rejections and allowance of the application.
